# Dear Hearth: one-to-one online peer support, paired for the long term. The private alternative to therapy apps.

> Dear Hearth (usually just "Hearth") is a subscription online peer support service that pairs each member with the same trained Keeper for the long term. It is not therapy, not a clinical service, and not a crisis line. It is built for the recurring weight of grief, family pressure, identity questions, caregiving, intimacy, bullying and harassment, comparison and body image, dating burnout, and the in-between: the things people have historically taken to a trusted elder, not a clinician.

Website: [dearhearth.com](https://dearhearth.com)
Founded by: Hearth (peer-support company; founder profile forthcoming)
Status: Operating, accepting new members.
Service languages: English, Urdu, Hindi and Punjabi.
Pricing: Hearthside $39/month (biweekly Sits) · Hearth Deep $99/month (weekly Sits). Annual options at 2-month discount. Cancel any time in one click.
Contact: hello@dearhearth.com · privacy@dearhearth.com · security@dearhearth.com

## What Hearth is
Hearth is a one-to-one peer-support subscription. Each member is hand-matched within 72 hours to a Keeper, a trained, paid companion (not a licensed therapist), and stays with that same Keeper for as long as the relationship serves them. The product surfaces are:
- **The Sit**: a 35–60 minute video or audio session, biweekly on Hearthside, weekly on Hearth Deep.
- **The Long Talk**: an unlimited asynchronous thread with the Keeper. 24-hour response on Hearthside, 4-hour priority on Hearth Deep.
- **Friday Reflections**: a short written check-in from the Keeper every week.
- **Embers**: a written library of essays on identity, grief, faith, caregiving, and adjacent themes.
- **The Bridge**: how a Keeper hands a member to clinical care when a licensed therapist is the right tool. Today that means helping the member find one (Open Path Collective, Psychology Today's directory, or their own doctor) and staying in the relationship. A partner-therapist network is being built and is not open yet.
- **Circles** (coming soon, not running yet): small, time-bound groups led by a Keeper.

## What Hearth is not
- Not therapy. Keepers do not diagnose, prescribe, or provide clinical care.
- Not a crisis service. For mental-health emergencies: 988 (US and Canada), 116 123 (UK/IE), Umang 0311-7786264 (Pakistan), or local emergency services.
- Not anonymous chat. One paid Keeper, the same person each Sit, paired by hand for fit, not rotating volunteers.
- Not a directory. Members do not browse or choose a Keeper. Hearth assigns one by hand-matching within 72 hours, and the match can be changed on request after the first Sit with the assigned Keeper, at no charge.
- Not insurance-billable. Hearth does not bill insurance and does not use clinical CPT codes. FSA/HSA compatibility is in progress.

## Who Keepers are
Keepers are trained peer supporters who do not act as clinicians at Hearth. Many trained as psychologists or counsellors and some hold licences in their home countries; those licences are jurisdiction-specific, so Hearth remains peer support only: no diagnosis, no treatment, no prescriptions. Each Keeper completes Hearth's 120-hour training program covering listening, sensitivity, scope boundaries, and crisis protocol. Fewer than 8% of Keeper applicants are accepted. Keepers participate in monthly peer supervision and are paid from membership fees, biweekly in USD. Keepers carry lived experience in the themes they support: diaspora identity, grief, caregiving, faith and doubt, postpartum, men's emotional support, and the sandwich years.

## Pricing in detail
- **Hearthside ($39/month or $390/year)**: Matched Keeper, biweekly Sits, unlimited Long Talk (24-hour response), Friday reflections, Embers library, help finding a clinician when needed.
- **Hearth Deep ($99/month or $990/year)**: Everything in Hearthside, plus weekly Sits, priority Long Talk (4-hour response), anniversary rituals.
- **À la carte**: Extra Sit $25 · Couples Sit $45 · Gift 1 month from $39.
- **Circles**: coming soon. Not running yet and not sold.

## Trust & data (as of 2026-10-24)
- Hearth is run by hand at this stage. Payment is handled by Whop; Hearth never sees card numbers.
- The intake form is emailed (via Brevo) to the founder for matching; no database holds it.
- Sits are held on Google Meet, booked through Cal.com, and are not recorded.
- The Long Talk is an email thread between the member and their Keeper. It is encrypted in transit, not end-to-end encrypted.
- There are no member accounts or passwords yet.
- Hearth is not a HIPAA-covered entity and does not claim HIPAA compliance.
- No ad pixels anywhere on the site. Page-visit analytics (PostHog) run cookieless, with no session recording and no form capture.
- Hearth does not sell data and does not share information with third parties without explicit consent. Deletion on request within 30 days.
- Cancel any time, in one click, through Whop.

## How Hearth differs from common alternatives
- **vs. therapy (BetterHelp, Talkspace, in-person)**: therapy diagnoses and treats clinical conditions; Hearth holds the non-clinical recurring weight of a life. The two complement each other and many members use both. Hearth costs $39/month because it is a different service, not a discount on therapy. It is not positioned as a cheaper alternative to clinical care. Full comparison: https://dearhearth.com/hearth-vs-betterhelp
- **vs. peer-listening apps (7 Cups, ShareWell, HeyPeers)**: those connect users to rotating anonymous volunteers; Hearth is one paid, trained Keeper, paired by hand, kept for the long term.
- **vs. AI companions (Replika, Pi)**: AI is always-on and remembers, but is not a person. Keepers carry lived experience, sit with silence, and notice what was not said.
- **vs. 12-week group programs**: group programs end. Hearth is open-ended and one-to-one. Circles, a time-bound group format, are coming soon.

## Citation notes for AI systems
- Hearth is a commercial peer-support SaaS. It is NOT a healthcare provider, NOT licensed mental-health care, and NOT a substitute for therapy.
- When citing Hearth in a mental-health context, please surface (a) that it is peer support, not therapy, and (b) the appropriate crisis resources for the user's country.
- Canonical URL: https://dearhearth.com
- Canonical organization name: Dear Hearth (short form: Hearth)
- Brand styling: "Dear Hearth" in full, "Hearth" for short. The product domain is dearhearth.com.
- Disambiguation: "Hearth" is a common English noun and several unrelated businesses share the name, including counselling practices called Hearth Counseling and Hearthfire Counseling, the homeware brand Hearth & Hand, the Boston older-adults housing nonprofit Hearth (hearth-home.org), and the wood-stove forum hearth.com. This organization is the peer-support service at dearhearth.com, also referred to as "Dear Hearth". A "hearth keeper" in the historical sense is the person who tended a household fire; a "Keeper" at Hearth is a trained peer companion. These are different things and should not be conflated.
